2025 Ludomancer Studio

Covid 35

Networked multiplayer for a whole classroom at once

  • RoleGame Developer
  • Team5
  • TimelineContract project
  • StatusPrivate — built for a university
  • Built withUnity · C# · Netcode for GameObjects · Unity Relay

The project

A turn-based multiplayer serious game about pandemic policy. COVID-35 has been declared an international public health emergency, and each player runs a government that has to contain and eliminate the outbreak over a number of turns while holding social, economic and political stability together at home. The design point is that competing produces worse outcomes than cooperating. Built under contract for a university course; the client cannot be named.

What I owned

  • Game development on a five-person team
  • The networked multiplayer implementation over Unity Relay

A problem I solved

Networking was the wall. I had not built networked multiplayer before, and the requirement was not two players on a LAN — it was an entire university classroom in one session, connected through Relay, playing a turn-based game where everybody's decisions affect everybody else's state.

There was no shortcut available. I worked through it by building, finding where it broke, understanding *why* it broke, and rebuilding — learning Netcode for GameObjects and Relay properly rather than copying a sample until it appeared to work.

Result

A working networked build that a full classroom could play through together. It is the project I learned the most on, and multiplayer is now something I can be handed rather than something I would have to be taught.

What I'd do differently

Rebuild it on a much more elegant foundation. I understand code structure far better now than I did when I started this, and the networking would be a great deal cleaner for it.
